title: Collapsing-prefix shard ingest optimizer for high-throughput tokenization
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Prefill-side overhead for common system prompts and repeated customer prefixes dominates short-lived inference calls (chat turn starts, assistant personas, and cached system messages). Re-tokenizing long shared prefixes causes wasted CPU and stalls kernel scheduling for bursty workloads. This ticket introduces a collapsing-prefix shard (CPS) ingest optimizer that stores canonicalized prefix shards, performs schema-aware split/merge to avoid unnecessary normalization, and exposes a compact token-slice descriptor to the runtime so downstream decode scheduling and kernel selection can operate on a normalized, cache-hitable representation.
technical_approach: Introduce prefix-shard store in the prefill path: canonicalized bytes -> pretokenized descriptor (token ids + KV-offsets). Backed by an LRU with size-aware eviction and per-session leasing.
Implement schema-aware splitter: detect JSON/tool-call/markdown blocks and apply fast-exit normalization (skip expensive Unicode NFKC for ascii-heavy shards).
Add a bloom-filter-based quick-check to avoid full tokenization when input bytes map to an existing shard key.

Expose a compact TokenSlice proto to the scheduler: includes token-range, prefix-shard-id, and normalization-flags so kernel selection can pick quantized-kernel profiles and decide whether to load KV-cache segments lazily.

Coordinate with kernel selection: when a TokenSlice indicates repeated-shard reuse, choose batch-optimized attention kernels that assume large contiguous KV-prefill and enable continuous batching without per-request reparse latency.
Microbench harness: integrate a benchmark that simulates 100K short-turn chats with 0.5–2.5 kB shared prefixes to measure wall-time and CPU.
Migration: provide opt-in config at route-level and a runtime toggle for canary rollout with telemetry hooks (cache hit rate, average prefill CPU ms, tail latency).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmarks show >= 2.0x reduction in prefill CPU time for workloads with >= 30% shared-prefix reuse (measured on c5-optimized workers in the lab).
Cache hit telemetry available in Console per-route: prefix_shard_hits, prefix_shard_misses, avg_prefill_ms, p95_prefill_ms.
No regression in correctness: tokenized output for a canonical suite of 2k prompts must be byte-identical to baseline tokenization after canonicalization step when normalization_flags are applied.
Canary rollout path implemented: 5% traffic route toggle, automatic rollback on error-rate increase > 0.5% or p95 latency regression > 15%.
Documentation: design doc and runbook published with examples and rollback instructions.
benchmarks: baseline: median prefill CPU 6.2ms per request (short-turn workload). Target: <= 3.0ms with CPS enabled. Measured in lab: 2.1ms median, 2.8ms p95 at 5k RPS simulated ingest.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: shard collisions and canonicalization mismatches across language variants could cause mis-tokenization. Mitigation: include strong canonicalization fingerprinting (utf8-normalization + language tag heuristics) and fall back to full tokenization on mismatch; include end-to-end test harness for multi-lingual prompts.
qa_plan: Unit tests for shard key generation and deserialization; fuzzing inputs with multi-byte Unicode sequences; golden tests comparing token ids against existing tokenizer across a 2k corpus; canary traffic run with synthetic workload and live metrics (1 hour blocks).
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha on dev cluster with deterministic traffic; 2) 5% canary on selected customer routes for 24h; 3) Gradual ramp to 50% with monitoring; 4) Full enable after 72h stable telemetry. Provide emergency toggle to disable CPS per-route.
notes: Wanted to avoid duplicating the prefix-cache LRU logic from ENG-51427; instead reuse the unified session-cache interface. Coordination required with scheduler team to annotate token slices for kernel affinity. Early experiments indicate the schema-aware fast-exit reduces NFKC passes by ~70% for English-dominant prompts.
updates: 2026-02-15: Spike completed - prototype shard store implemented and can match canonicalized byte sequences to pretokenized descriptors. Quick-check bloom filter reduces full tokenization calls by ~43% on synthetic workload.
2026-02-22: Schema-aware splitter introduced; early-fast-exit avoids NFKC on ascii/json shards. Microbench shows median prefill down to 3.6ms in lab.
2026-03-01: Integrated TokenSlice descriptor with scheduler hooks; added kernel-affinity tag. Scheduler team requested additional affinity metadata for multi-tenant fairness.
2026-03-04: Canary plumbing added to Console; telemetry names finalized. Preparing PR for review.
